# After integrating the foot IMU, the IMU estimation drifts; what else should be checked besides the filter parameters?

> **Current answer:** Check the time offset and rotation extrinsic parameters of the foot IMU and joint encoders, and verify that the calibration actions provide sufficient triaxial excitation. The candidate approach for A2I-Calib is to minimize the condition number of the foot end angular velocity covariance and actively execute the calibration trajectory; the effect should be verified independently in the paper/code.

## Possible causes

- IMU/encoder time offset, incorrect rotation extrinsic parameters, insufficient regular gait excitation, and noise amplification.

## Attempts

- Optimize the condition number of the foot end angular velocity covariance, generate sine/cosine basis function trajectories, and use RL controllers to stabilize and actively execute the calibration trajectory.
